title: Gabber approximation preserves thickened associated graded algebras
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent henselian Noetherian local ring, let $\widehat A$ be its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion, and write $\widehat A=\varinjlim_\alpha A_\alpha$ as a directed union of finite type $A$-subalgebras with inclusions $s_\alpha:A_\alpha\to\widehat A$ [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ be of finite type and let $X_{\alpha_0}\to\operatorname{Spec}A_{\alpha_0}$ be a fixed finite type model, equipped with an isomorphism $X\cong X_{\alpha_0}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_{\alpha_0}}\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $\alpha\ge\alpha_0$ define $X_\alpha$ by base change of this model. For an $A$-algebra map $u:A_\alpha\to A$ put $X_u=X_\alpha\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_\alpha}S$. For any $S$-scheme $T$, write $I_T=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_T$, $T^{[a]}=(T,\mathcal O_T/I_T^a)$ for its closed subscheme defined by $I_T^a$, and
$$G_a(T)=\bigoplus_{q\in\mathbf Z} I_T^q/I_T^{q+a},\qquad I_T^q=\mathcal O_T\text{ for }q\le0.$$
Here $a\ge1$, the summands are in degree $q$, and multiplication is induced by multiplication of ideals; thus $G_a(T)$ is a graded sheaf of algebras on $T^{[a]}$. The same formula for $(A,\mathfrak m)$ defines the base graded ring $G_a(A)$. There are $\alpha_1\ge\alpha_0$ and integers $n_0\ge c\ge1$ such that for every $\alpha\ge\alpha_1$, $N\ge n_0+1$, and $u$ whose composite with $A\to\widehat A$ is congruent to $s_\alpha$ modulo $\mathfrak m^N\widehat A$, with $a=N-c$, the canonical isomorphism
$$\phi:X^{[a]}\xrightarrow{\sim}X_u^{[a]}$$
induced by that congruence extends uniquely to an isomorphism
$$\phi^{-1}G_a(X_u)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_a(X)$$
of graded $G_a(A)$-algebras. In particular the isomorphism in degree zero is the given $\phi$. No regularity, flatness, or normality of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose III section 4, Definition 4.2 (pp.39--40), and Theorem 5.1 (pp.41--42), with section 2 for the fixed-model conventions; in the ancestor finiteness/duality branch this is the approximation input in III Proposition 6.2, p.44, immediately before conditions a) and b). The exponent here is N=n+1 and a=N-c.

proof.text: First identify $A/\mathfrak m^k$ with $\widehat A/\mathfrak m^k\widehat A$ for every $k\geq1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] to $A\twoheadrightarrow A/\mathfrak m^k$. Its image maximal ideal has kth power zero, so its completion is the ring itself: a compatible sequence is constant after index $k$. The lemma therefore gives exactly this canonical quotient isomorphism. Restricting this isomorphism from exponent $q+a$ to exponent $q$ identifies the kernels $\mathfrak m^q/\mathfrak m^{q+a}$ for $q>0$; for $q\leq0$ use the same quotient formula or the zero module. Hence $G_a(A)\cong G_a(\widehat A)$ canonically. Congruent maps modulo $\mathfrak m^N$ induce equal maps to $A/\mathfrak m^a$ whenever $1\leq a\leq N$. The fibre-product universal property then supplies the stated canonical $\phi$ on these thickenings.

source.place: III section 2, pp.35--36, (2.b); Stacks Tag 00MA, lemma-completion-tensor, quotient specialization

proof.text: Fix a finite affine cover $U_{i,\alpha_0}=\operatorname{Spec}C_{i,\alpha_0}$ of the given model, with each $C_{i,\alpha_0}$ finite type over $A_{\alpha_0}$, as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $A_{\alpha_0}$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], write $C_{i,\alpha_0}=A_{\alpha_0}[t_1,\ldots,t_{d_i}]/(P_{i,1},\ldots,P_{i,b_i})$. Base change gives the same polynomial presentation: maps out of the quotient are precisely choices of the variable images satisfying the displayed relations, and this description is preserved by scalar extension. This identifies every later chart and its completed chart. Only charts of the given model are used; no new scheme model or descent of an affine cover is required.

The ring $\widehat A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and $B_i=\widehat A[t_1,\ldots,t_{d_i}]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Regard $P_i$ as a row $B_i^{b_i}\to B_i$. Its kernel is a submodule of a finite free module, hence finitely generated by [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented]. Choose generators as the columns of a matrix $R_i:B_i^{e_i}\to B_i^{b_i}$. Thus $\operatorname{im}R_i=\ker P_i$. This asserts exactness only over $B_i$, not over any intermediate coefficient algebra.

There are finitely many coefficients in all matrices $R_i$. Since the subalgebras form a directed union, choose one $\alpha_1\geq\alpha_0$ containing them. Let $R_{i,\alpha}$ denote these same polynomial matrices at every $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$, and let $P_{i,\alpha}$ be the rows already fixed by the model. The equations $P_iR_i=0$ hold coefficientwise in $\widehat A$, so they hold in $A_\alpha$ because $A_\alpha\hookrightarrow\widehat A$ is injective. Applying any $u$ gives $P_{i,u}R_{i,u}=0$ over $A[t]$ and over $B_i$. No exactness of $R_{i,\alpha},P_{i,\alpha}$ is needed.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to the image submodules of $R_i$ and $P_i$, with ideal $I_i=\mathfrak mB_i$. An image element in $I_i^j$ is, for $j\geq c_i$, an $I_i^{j-c_i}$-linear combination of image elements, so lifting these finitely many terms gives the image bounds required by the perturbation lemma used next. Enlarge all constants to one $c\geq1$, which is permitted by the Artin-Rees statement, and take $n_0=c$. The rings, matrices and constants are fixed independently of $\alpha,N,u$.

Let $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$, $N\geq n_0+1$ and $u$ satisfy the prescribed congruence, and put $n=N-1$ and $a=N-c$. Then $n\geq c$ and $a\geq1$. Set $P_i'=s(P_{i,u})$ and $R_i'=s(R_{i,u})$ over $B_i$. Every matrix coefficient difference belongs to $\mathfrak m^N\widehat A$, so the two map differences take values in $I_i^{n+1}$ times their target modules. Their product is zero by step 4. Thus [lem-per-higher-graded-cokernel-perturbation] applies with $F=B_i$, giving the identity-induced isomorphism $G_a(B_i/(P_i'))\cong G_a(B_i/(P_i))$. It preserves multiplication and is linear over $G_a(B_i)$, hence over $G_a(A)$. In degree zero it is the quotient identification obtained by reducing the given congruence, so agrees with $\phi$ on the completed affine chart.

Write $C_{i,u}=A[t]/(P_{i,u})$. For every $k\geq1$, step 1 and the polynomial quotient presentation identify $C_{i,u}/\mathfrak m^kC_{i,u}$ with $(B_i/(P_i'))/\mathfrak m^k(B_i/(P_i'))$: both are $(A/\mathfrak m^k)[t]/(P_{i,u}\bmod\mathfrak m^k)$. Taking kernels of the maps from exponent $q+a$ to exponent $q$ gives the same comparison for every positive-degree summand; negative degrees are quotients or zero. These comparisons preserve products because all maps come from the displayed polynomial quotient maps. The higher graded algebra on the algebraic chart therefore equals that on its completed base change. The isomorphism of step 6 consequently gives the required graded algebra isomorphism on each chart of the identified thickening. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] these quotient formulas localize on basic opens, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] identifies their kernel subquotients after localization. Thus these are isomorphisms of the indicated graded sheaves, compatible with restriction.

For any $S$-scheme $T$, $G_a(T)$ is generated as a graded $G_a(A)$-algebra by its degree-zero sheaf $\mathcal O_T/I_T^a$. Indeed, locally every element of $I_T^q$ for $q>0$ is a finite sum $\sum_j b_jv_j$ with $b_j\in\mathfrak m^q$ and $v_j\in\mathcal O_T$; its degree-$q$ quotient class is the sum of products of the degree-$q$ base classes of $b_j$ and the degree-zero classes of $v_j$. For $-a<q\leq0$, a representative $v$ is the product of the degree-$q$ base class of $1$ and the degree-zero class of $v$. For $q\leq-a$ the summand is zero. Thus two graded maps linear over $G_a(A)$ and agreeing in degree zero agree on every section locally and are equal. This argument works on all open restrictions.

On the intersection of two chart thickenings, the maps constructed in step 7 have the same degree-zero map, namely the restriction of $\phi$, and the same structural base map. Step 8 makes these restrictions equal, even when the intersection is not affine. Therefore the local sheaf maps glue to a graded $G_a(A)$-algebra map $\phi^{-1}G_a(X_u)\to G_a(X)$. Their inverses agree for the same reason and glue to its inverse. Step 8 also proves uniqueness of the global extension. The finite chart cover supplied one common $\alpha_1,c,n_0$, so the result holds simultaneously for every indicated $\alpha,N,u$. For the empty model use the empty sheaf map and take $\alpha_1=\alpha_0$, $c=n_0=1$.

split_report.summary: Read ILO III 2, 4.2, 4.5 and 5.1. Kept the statement, constructed fixed-model affine presentations and finite syzygy matrices, descended only their finite coefficients, chose uniform Artin-Rees bounds, compared higher graded cokernels and algebraic versus completed charts, and proved uniqueness and gluing explicitly. One smaller algebraic perturbation statement is new; all Noetherianity, finite-module and completion tools are existing nodes.
